- I must approve the project before interviews begin

- Using personal phones for recording (data privacy/security)
- Indefinite retention of files

transcript.text: Good morning, Dr. Morgan. Thank you for gathering us. Let me walk you through where the plan currently stands. As drafted, the proposal calls for 20 student interviewers who would use their personal phones to record interviews with community members about local history. The recordings would then be published on the public school website and retained indefinitely. I share your concerns about privacy, consent, and data security, and I think there are some important adjustments we should consider before this moves forward. One thing I want to flag early is that we need to make sure we're following district policy on which students are eligible to conduct recorded interviews — there are training requirements that must be met first. I have the roster details if the group would like to review that now.

transcript.text: I've completed the technology review for this project, and there are several requirements the draft plan doesn't currently meet. Personal phones cannot be used for school recordings — the project must use district tablets instead. All files must be stored in the restricted OralHistory drive, not on personal devices or public servers. Recordings must be deleted exactly 45 days after the final class presentation — indefinite retention is not permitted. Finally, the technology plan must include a secure-storage configuration record documenting these arrangements.
